status_summary: The 2022 Charter Schools Program priorities and requirements (final rule of 2022-07-06) have not been formally rescinded, but ED has stopped applying them. The FY2025 State Entity and CMO notices of 2025-01-21 used the 2022 requirements, including a needs analysis of effects on school diversity and safeguards on for-profit management; ED withdrew both on 2025-02-04 to align priorities with the administration and minimize oversight. Reissued FY2025 notices (2025-05-09 to 2025-05-16) rely on the 2018 final priorities, and the CMO notice has no absolute priority; ED raised FY2025 program funding to $500 million in May 2025, and the FY2026 State Entity notice of 2026-04-20 does not cite the 2022 rule. The stage is implemented because the 2022 terms are no longer applied in practice, while the rule itself remains on the books and could be used again.

timeline.event: ED published final priorities, requirements, definitions and selection criteria for CSP State Entity, CMO and Developer grants (the 2022 rule the Mandate targets, proposed 2022-03-14).

ED published FY2025 CMO and State Entity competition notices that applied the 2022 requirements, including a diversity needs analysis, a desegregation assurance and safeguards for contracts with for-profit managers.

ED withdrew the FY2025 State Entity and CMO notices and cancelled those competitions, citing alignment with administration priorities and executive orders and an intent to minimize unnecessary oversight.
ED published a new FY2025 State Entity notice.

ED published a new FY2025 CMO notice that cites only the 2018 final priorities, has no absolute priority, and estimates $72 million with a competitive preference for reopening low-performing schools as charters.

Education Week reported that ED added $60 million to bring FY2025 CSP funding to $500 million and launched a model development grant program, describing the withdrawn notices as containing excessive regulatory burdens.
ED published final supplemental priorities on literacy, education choice and returning education to the states, replacing Secretary's supplemental priorities published before 2025-01-20.

ED announced a record $500 million in Charter Schools Program awards across State Entity, CMO, facilities, credit enhancement, model development and developer grants (page last reviewed on this date).

ED published the FY2026 State Entity competition notice, solicited through the Labor Department, with an authorizer best-practices absolute priority and seven competitive preference priorities including Returning Education to the States and Expanding Education Choice; the notice does not cite the 2022 rule.

title: Rescind the 2022 Charter School Program priorities and reduce federal charter restrictions
uncertainties: A Federal Register API search for Charter Schools Program priorities from 2022 found the 2022 final rule and no notice rescinding it. The FY2026 State Entity notice refers to grant materials on the ED website and Grants.gov for full requirements, which were not read, so whether any 2022 requirement still applies there is not confirmed. The May 2025 State Entity notice was identified by the API search but not opened. The ED awards release has no announcement date (page last reviewed 2025-09-24). The Mandate cites the 2022 proposed priorities; the final rule of 2022-07-06 is treated as the regulation it targets. FY2026 appropriations for the program were not checked.
